MC-1.why_it_is_a_contradiction_and_not_a_pref: commercial_status DEFAULT is 'active' (0068:34). COMMERCIAL_STATE_MACHINE.canonicity: OD-1. There is exactly ONE commercial state machine. Its single carrier is commercial_accounts.commercial_status. No second state is derived from a Stripe column, from organizations.status, from the presence of a subscription id, or from a plan label. A reader that needs commercial state reads this column and nothing else.
COMMERCIAL_STATE_MACHINE.separation_preserved: organizations.status is the tenant-operational control and is NEVER written by this machine, in either direction (PI-1, preserved). Commercial suspension and tenant suspension remain two verbs with two authorities.
COMMERCIAL_STATE_MACHINE.carrier_scope: The machine is CommercialAccount-scoped. An account governing several Organizations has ONE commercial state; its entitlement effects are applied per Organization, because entitlement is Organization-scoped by CE-3's effective_key and CA-08's no-pooled-quota rule. One state, N applications - never one pooled entitlement.
COMMERCIAL_STATE_MACHINE.closed_world: The six states below are the complete set. A value outside them is a violation, not an extension, and the widened CHECK of FUTURE_DDL.D-1 is what makes that structurally true rather than merely intended.

states.meaning: Non-commercial. The account exists, no commercial relationship is live, and nothing has been sold. This is the DEFAULT and the state every account is born in.
enter_events: CommercialAccount creation (the DEFAULT of the widened column).
CE-4 backfill seeding of a pre-existing Organization that has no Stripe identity.
Cancellation completing from ACTIVE_STRIPE, PAST_DUE or SUSPENDED (OD-6): the correct bootstrap / non-commercial landing state.
exit_events: -> ACTIVE_STRIPE: a first-party binding completed AND a subscription observed in Stripe status active or trialing.
-> CLOSED: an authorized platform-admin account closure.
states.commercial_access_result: NON_COMMERCIAL. The tenant may sign in, may read all of its own historical evidence, reports and audit history, and may exercise every capability whose grant source is BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT. No PLAN capability is available.
states.entitlement_result: Live grants of source BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT only. Any live PLAN grant is CLOSED on entry to this state. No PLAN grant may be opened while in it.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_subscription_id MUST be NULL. stripe_customer_id MAY be non-NULL and is RETAINED across cancellation - the customer relationship survives the subscription (OD-6 clears the SUBSCRIPTION identity, not the customer identity; retaining it is what makes reactivation idempotent rather than a second customer).
states.manual_activation_eligibility: ELIGIBLE. This is the only state from which manual activation is a normal transition rather than a correction.
states.audit_effect: action commercial.state.entered, entity_type commercial_account, before_json and after_json carrying the prior and new state, reason naming the cause. Entry by DEFAULT at creation is audited by the creating verb, not by a trigger.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, 'BOOTSTRAP', cause_identity) where cause_identity is the Stripe event_id for a cancellation-caused entry and the creating audit_log id otherwise. Re-entering BOOTSTRAP when already in BOOTSTRAP is a NO-OP, never a second audit row.
states.ordering_rules: A transition into BOOTSTRAP caused by a Stripe event is subject to ORD-1..ORD-6 in full. A transition caused by an admin verb is ordered by the per-account advisory lock alone.

states.meaning: A live, paid, current commercial relationship backed by a Stripe subscription.
enter_events: From BOOTSTRAP: subscription observed active or trialing after a first-party binding.
From PAST_DUE: recovery, i.e. a subscription observed active, or an invoice observed paid for the subscription (OD-4 - past_due is recoverable and recovery returns here).
From SUSPENDED: reactivation of the SAME subscription observed active. See REACTIVATION.
exit_events: -> PAST_DUE: subscription observed past_due, or an invoice payment failure observed for the subscription.
-> BOOTSTRAP: subscription observed canceled or deleted (OD-6).
-> ACTIVE_STRIPE (self): a subscription replacement or plan change. See SUBSCRIPTION_REPLACEMENT.
states.commercial_access_result: FULL. Every capability the live plan grants is available at its granted limit.
states.entitlement_result: Live grants of source PLAN, opened by governed re-evaluation with plan_ref SNAPSHOTTED at grant time (CE-3 plan_snapshot_rule, preserved). BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT grants for the same capability_key are CLOSED first - CE-3 permits exactly one live grant per (organization_id, capability_key) and the partial unique index enforces it.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_customer_id NOT NULL. stripe_subscription_id NOT NULL. The persisted subscription status MUST be active or trialing.
states.manual_activation_eligibility: NOT ELIGIBLE. Manual activation into a state already backed by Stripe would create two commercial bases for one account. A platform operator who needs to override a limit while Stripe is live uses a COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION grant (PAYMENT_SUSPENSION, preserved), which is an entitlement act, not a state act.
states.audit_effect: commercial.state.entered plus, separately, the entitlement re-evaluation's own audit rows. Two acts, two audit rows, per PLAN_ENTITLEMENT_BOUNDARY - a single row covering both would re-create the CC-3 fusion.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, stripe_subscription_id, stripe_event_id). The ledger's event_id PRIMARY KEY already makes the Stripe side idempotent; this key makes the STATE side idempotent for non-Stripe causes too.
states.ordering_rules: ORD-1..ORD-6 in full. An event that would enter ACTIVE_STRIPE but is stale under ORD-3 is refused, not applied.

states.meaning: Payment has failed and the relationship is RECOVERABLE. Capacity is deliberately retained (OD-4).
enter_events: From ACTIVE_STRIPE: subscription observed past_due, or an invoice payment failure observed for the subscription.
exit_events: -> ACTIVE_STRIPE: recovery (subscription active, or invoice paid).
-> SUSPENDED: subscription observed unpaid, i.e. Stripe has exhausted its dunning and the relationship is no longer recoverable (OD-5).
-> BOOTSTRAP: subscription observed canceled or deleted while past_due (OD-6).
states.commercial_access_result: FULL, UNCHANGED FROM ACTIVE_STRIPE. This is OD-4 and it is the single most easily lost clause of this authority: entering PAST_DUE has NO product effect. It changes what the platform knows and what it may tell the tenant; it changes nothing the tenant may do.
states.entitlement_result: NO GRANT IS TOUCHED. No grant is closed, no limit is reduced, no replacement row is written. An implementation that closes or downgrades a grant on entry to PAST_DUE has violated OD-4 regardless of how briefly.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_customer_id NOT NULL, stripe_subscription_id NOT NULL, persisted subscription status past_due.
states.manual_activation_eligibility: NOT ELIGIBLE. A live subscription exists; see ACTIVE_STRIPE. An operator extending goodwill beyond Stripe's dunning uses a COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION grant.
states.audit_effect: commercial.state.entered ONLY. The absence of a companion entitlement audit row is itself the evidence that OD-4 was honoured, and MC-T-PAST-DUE tests exactly that absence.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, stripe_subscription_id, stripe_event_id). Repeated past_due notifications for the same subscription re-enter no state and write no second audit row.
states.ordering_rules: ORD-1..ORD-6. Note the asymmetry ORD-6 exists for: a stale past_due arriving after a completed recovery must NOT re-enter PAST_DUE.
states.duration_is_not_frozen: How long an account may remain in PAST_DUE is NOT ratified here and is NOT a Uellix timer. PAYMENT_SUSPENSION.grace_period leaves collections timing to future configurable policy, and the transition out of PAST_DUE is driven by OBSERVED Stripe state, never by an elapsed Uellix clock. An implementation that hard-codes a grace window into the entitlement path has exceeded this authority and the preserved one alike.

states.meaning: Payment has definitively failed (Stripe unpaid). Commercial capacity is CLOSED; the record is not (OD-5).
enter_events: From PAST_DUE or ACTIVE_STRIPE: subscription observed unpaid.
exit_events: -> ACTIVE_STRIPE: the same subscription observed active again (reactivation).
-> BOOTSTRAP: subscription observed canceled or deleted (OD-6).
states.commercial_access_result: CLOSED FOR PAID CAPACITY, OPEN FOR RECORD. The tenant retains sign-in, retains membership, retains role, and retains READ access to all of its own historical evidence, reports and audit history. PAYMENT_SUSPENSION.read_side_rule is preserved verbatim: loss of a paid capability is loss of the capability, not of the record.
states.entitlement_result: Every live PLAN grant is CLOSED (effective_to set once, per CE-3 append_only_rule). Where the capability has a BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT entitlement, a replacement row of source BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT MAY be opened; where it does not, the capability is simply absent and the evaluator fails closed. Revocation is EXPLICIT, AUDITABLE and names the commercial cause, per PAYMENT_SUSPENSION, preserved.
states.not_tenant_suspension: organizations.status is NOT written. Membership is NOT deleted. Tenant identity is NOT destroyed. Evidence is NOT destroyed.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_customer_id NOT NULL, stripe_subscription_id NOT NULL and RETAINED (this is what makes reactivation of the same subscription distinguishable from a new one), persisted subscription status unpaid.
states.manual_activation_eligibility: NOT ELIGIBLE while a subscription id is retained. An account whose subscription is later canceled lands in BOOTSTRAP and becomes eligible there. This ordering is deliberate: manual activation must never be a way to paper over an unpaid live subscription.
states.audit_effect: commercial.state.entered, plus one entitlement audit row PER CLOSED GRANT naming the commercial cause. Two authorities, two acts, separately audited.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, stripe_subscription_id, stripe_event_id) for the state; (organization_id, capability_key, closing_event_identity) for each grant closure. A redelivered unpaid event finds every grant already closed and closes nothing a second time - CE-3 forbids a second UPDATE of effective_to, so the second attempt is a refusal, not a rewrite.

states.meaning: A live commercial relationship NOT backed by a Stripe subscription - an invoiced, contracted, granted or otherwise off-Stripe arrangement. Reachable ONLY by explicitly authorized manual activation (OD-7).
enter_events: From BOOTSTRAP: an authorized manual activation verb, executed by a platform principal, carrying an actor, a reason and a review horizon.
exit_events: -> BOOTSTRAP: authorized manual deactivation, or the review horizon expiring without renewal.
-> ACTIVE_STRIPE: a first-party binding completing and a Stripe subscription becoming active. The manual basis is closed in the same governed act that opens the Stripe basis; the two never coexist.
states.commercial_access_result: FULL, at the limits the manual activation names. Identical in product effect to ACTIVE_STRIPE; distinct in commercial basis and therefore in audit, in reporting and in what an operator may infer.
states.entitlement_result: Live grants of source COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION, carrying commercial_account_id NOT NULL (CE-3's CHECK requires exactly that for this source), an actor, a reason and an effective period. NOT source PLAN: there is no plan. NOT source PLATFORM_ADMIN: CE-3's CHECK forbids a commercial_account_id on that source, and an off-Stripe commercial arrangement HAS a commercial basis. This is why COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION is the correct source and the other three are wrong.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_subscription_id MUST be NULL. A non-NULL subscription id in this state is a violation and the state verb refuses it. stripe_customer_id MAY be non-NULL (an account that once paid by card and now invoices keeps its customer identity).
states.manual_activation_eligibility: ALREADY ACTIVATED. Re-activation is a NO-OP under the idempotency key; RENEWAL of the review horizon is a distinct, separately audited verb.
states.audit_effect: commercial.manual_activation with a MANDATORY non-NULL actor_user_id, a MANDATORY reason, and the review horizon in after_json. There is no unaudited override (PAYMENT_SUSPENSION, preserved), and unlike a Stripe-caused transition the actor here MUST be a person: stella_0005c's reasoning applied from the other side - a decision a human made must not be attributed to a machine, exactly as a machine's must not be attributed to a human.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, 'MANUAL_ACTIVATION', authorization_reference). The authorization_reference is the platform-admin decision identity; two executions of the same authorization produce one activation.
states.ordering_rules: Not Stripe-ordered - no source event exists. Ordered by the per-account advisory lock. A Stripe event that arrives for an account in this state and carries a subscription id is REFUSED with cause manual_basis_conflict and escalates; it does not silently convert the account.

states.meaning: Terminal. The commercial relationship is over and the account is not to be reused.
enter_events: From any state: an authorized platform-admin account closure verb.
exit_events: NONE. CLOSED is terminal. A tenant returning commercially receives a NEW CommercialAccount; the FK ON DELETE RESTRICT of 0068:41 already guarantees a closed account that still governs a live Organization cannot be deleted, so terminality costs no history.
states.commercial_access_result: CLOSED FOR PAID CAPACITY, OPEN FOR RECORD, exactly as SUSPENDED. Closure is a commercial act, never a data-destruction act.
states.entitlement_result: Every live grant of every source is CLOSED, including BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT. An Organization still governed by a CLOSED account and still operationally live is a governance anomaly that ESCALATES; this authority does not silently re-home it.
states.stripe_requirements: stripe_subscription_id MUST be NULL on entry (the closure verb cancels or refuses). stripe_customer_id is RETAINED for the record.
states.manual_activation_eligibility: NOT ELIGIBLE, in any circumstance. Terminal means terminal.
states.audit_effect: commercial.account.closed with mandatory actor and reason, plus one entitlement audit row per closed grant.
states.idempotency_key: (commercial_account_id, 'CLOSED'). Closing a CLOSED account is a NO-OP.
states.ordering_rules: Ordered by the per-account advisory lock. ANY Stripe event arriving for a CLOSED account is recorded in the ledger and terminally IGNORED with cause account_closed; it is never applied, and it is never a reason to leave CLOSED.

transition_table_closure.rule: A transition not listed as an exit_event of the source state and an enter_event of the target state DOES NOT EXIST. The state verb enumerates the legal pairs and refuses everything else with cause illegal_transition. An enumeration is what makes 'fail closed' true rather than hoped for.
forbidden_pairs_worth_naming: BOOTSTRAP -> ACTIVE_STRIPE without a completed first-party binding. OD-2, OD-3.
any -> ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE from a state other than BOOTSTRAP. OD-7.
any -> any, caused by a Stripe webhook, that also writes an entitlement_grants row in the same transaction. STRIPE_BOUNDARY.webhook_prohibitions, preserved.

ENTITLEMENT_CONTRACT.EC-1_source_of_limit: The live EntitlementGrant is the sole source of a runtime limit, per USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY, preserved. The commercial state machine NEVER writes a limit. It writes a STATE, and the state's effect on entitlement is realised by the governed entitlement writer of CE-5 and by no other writer.
ENTITLEMENT_CONTRACT.EC-2_two_acts_never_one: A commercial state write and an entitlement write are two acts in two authorities, each separately audited, the second refusable. A transaction performing both is PROHIBITED regardless of code factoring - STRIPE_BOUNDARY.downstream_reaction, preserved and extended here from webhooks to EVERY cause including manual activation.
ENTITLEMENT_CONTRACT.EC-3_emission: A commercial state transition EMITS a governed re-evaluation request, recorded in the same transaction as the state write (it is a request row, not an effect) and consumed by the CE-5 entitlement writer in a SEPARATE transaction. See FUTURE_DDL.D-4.

EC-4_closing_conjunction.rule: The EFFECTIVE entitlement for (organization, capability) is the live grant CONJOINED with the commercial gate of the governing account's state. The gate can only ever REDUCE. It can never create, raise or extend a limit.
EC-4_closing_conjunction.gate_values: BOOTSTRAP -> pass-through (grants of source BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT are unaffected; a stale PLAN grant is gated to BLOCKED). ACTIVE_STRIPE, ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE, PAST_DUE -> pass-through. SUSPENDED, CLOSED -> BLOCKED.
EC-4_closing_conjunction.why_it_exists: EC-3 makes the entitlement effect ASYNCHRONOUS to the state write. Without EC-4 the window between them fails OPEN: the account is SUSPENDED and the grant is still live, so a suspended tenant keeps spending. The conjunction closes that window without making the webhook write a grant.
EC-4_closing_conjunction.why_it_does_not_violate_PLAN_ENTITLEMENT: That boundary forbids a code path in which reading a PLAN value produces an effective limit WITHOUT an intervening grant row. A monotonically reducing gate produces no limit from any plan value; with no grant row the conjunction is empty and the evaluator still fails closed. The prohibited direction is creation, and this gate cannot create.
EC-4_closing_conjunction.not_a_second_source_of_truth: The gate reads commercial_status, which OD-1 makes the single canonical state. It is one source read at two moments, not two sources.

EC-5_NO_LEGACY_FREE.rule: There is NO free tier of ten. Cancellation, suspension and closure yield limit_kind BLOCKED, which projects to stella_monthly_quota 0, per USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY.limit_projection, preserved.
prohibitions: mapStripePriceToQuota MUST NOT appear on any write path. Its display-only admissibility is already the preserved STRIPE_BOUNDARY.unknown_price_rule; this extends the same rule to the null-price case that rule's existing guard misses (MC-4).
A null or absent price MUST NOT be resolved to a quota AT ALL. Cancellation is a state transition, not a price lookup.
STRIPE_QUOTAS.free MUST NOT be reachable from any grant, any projection, any state effect or any enforcement read.

A capability with no declared metered semantic FAILS CLOSED. USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY.null_semantic_prohibition is preserved: the null-means-unlimited overload is retained for the Stella capability ALONE and is not a general rule.
EC-5_NO_LEGACY_FREE.test_obligation: A negative control asserts that no write path reaches the value 10 from a cancellation, and a mutation control asserts that restoring the legacy fallback turns that control RED.

EC-6_pre_CE4_interim_rule.measured_precondition: entitlement_grants does not exist and every organizations.commercial_account_id is NULL (R-05).
EC-6_pre_CE4_interim_rule.rule: The CE-3 evaluator MUST NOT be wired into any enforcement path before CE-4 has seeded accounts, associations and grants. Wired earlier it denies every Organization - not as a bug but as its correct fail-closed behaviour on empty inputs.
EC-6_pre_CE4_interim_rule.consequence_for_sequencing: Every implementation package below that CHANGES an enforcement decision is gated on CE-4. Packages that build substrate are not.

ENTITLEMENT_CONTRACT.EC-7_no_pooled_quota: Preserved verbatim from USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY: there is no shared live quota pool in Commercial V1. Exhaustion in one Organization has no effect on any sibling under the same CommercialAccount. One commercial state, N independent Organization-scoped entitlements.

STRIPE_FIRST_BINDING.origin: The binding originates from the CommercialAccount, first-party authenticated, BEFORE any checkout exists.

verb.name: governed first-binding verb (bind_commercial_stripe_customer)
verb.precondition: The caller is authenticated, holds an organization-admin-or-above role in an Organization governed by the target CommercialAccount, and the account's stripe_customer_id is NULL.
verb.act: Create a Stripe Customer via the Stripe API with an idempotency key derived from commercial_account_id, then persist the RETURNED customer id onto commercial_accounts.stripe_customer_id.
verb.idempotency_key: commercial_account_id. This is the whole of OD-2's 'idempotently': a retried, duplicated or concurrent first binding for the same account yields the SAME Stripe Customer, never a second one. Stripe's own idempotency window bounds the API side; the UNIQUE constraint of FUTURE_DDL.D-2 bounds the database side; the per-account advisory lock bounds the concurrent side. Three bounds because each fails differently.
refusals: stripe_customer_id already non-NULL -> NO-OP, return the existing id. Not an error: OD-2 says idempotent.
the Stripe API returns a customer id already bound to a DIFFERENT commercial_account -> refusal and ESCALATION. See the attack below.

customer_id_is_never_client_supplied.rule: NO API surface, server action, form field, query parameter or webhook payload may supply a Stripe customer id that becomes a binding. The only admissible source is the value RETURNED by the platform's own customers.create call.
customer_id_is_never_client_supplied.preserved_reasoning: This is the same reasoning that removed the checkout.session.completed branch: client_reference_id is buyer-supplied and 'a value an attacker chooses cannot be the anchor of a tenancy bound' (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:238-240). The rule is generalised here from that one field to every inbound path.

cross_tenant_binding_attack.threat: An organization admin binds a Stripe customer id belonging to ANOTHER account - by guessing it, by reading it from an invoice, or by replaying it - and thereby attaches a foreign paying subscription to their own tenant.
cross_tenant_binding_attack.measured_exposure_today: F11 recorded this as Tier-A because no binding path is governed. Measured here: no binding path EXISTS at all (R-08), so the exposure at AS_OF is latent rather than live. It becomes live the moment a binding path is added without these controls.
defence_in_depth: D1 no client-supplied id (above) - the attacker has no field to put it in.
D2 UNIQUE(stripe_customer_id) on commercial_accounts (FUTURE_DDL.D-2) - if a path is ever added, the second account claiming the id fails at the database, not at a check someone can forget.
D4 the webhook resolves WHICH account an event addresses from the Stripe identity columns ONLY, never from a buyer-supplied checkout field (STRIPE_BOUNDARY.identity_rule, preserved).
D5 refusal plus escalation on a detected collision - a collision is evidence of either an attack or a corrupted binding and neither may be auto-resolved.
cross_tenant_binding_attack.why_four_controls_and_not_one: D1 is code and can be regressed by a refactor. D2 and D3 are schema and survive a refactor. D4 bounds the read side, which D1 to D3 do not touch. D5 makes the failure loud. A single control here would be a single point of silent failure on a Tier-A path.

CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY.rule: Checkout is admissible ONLY for an account that ALREADY has a bound stripe_customer_id. The checkout session is created with that customer, and it establishes NO identity of its own.
CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY.success_url_carries_nothing: success_url is a REDIRECT TARGET and nothing else. It MUST NOT carry, encode or imply account identity, organization identity, plan identity or entitlement. A success_url that is trusted for identity is a buyer-supplied binding wearing a different hat.
CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY.webhook_cannot_bind: Preserved and restated: 'First binding remains first-party authenticated. A webhook never establishes a binding it did not already have' (STRIPE_BOUNDARY.target). checkout.session.completed remains RECORDED, NEVER APPLIED - lib/capabilities/stripe-webhook.ts:261-273 already returns not_applicable with reason first_binding_requires_first_party_flow, and that disposition is FROZEN by this authority rather than merely inherited.
CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY.ordering_of_the_journey: bind (first-party, idempotent) -> checkout (Stripe-hosted, identity-free) -> subscription event (webhook, applied to an ALREADY KNOWN account) -> state transition -> emitted re-evaluation -> grant write. Six steps, five boundaries. The first binding is step one precisely so that no later step ever has to invent identity.
CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY.portal_deadlock_resolution: app/app/organization/billing/actions.ts:20-34 gates the portal on an id nothing can write (R-08). Once the first-binding verb exists, the portal's else branch becomes reachable-by-construction and its 'contact sales' throw is replaced by the bind-then-checkout journey. This authority states the target; the replacement itself is CB-4.

source_of_truth.rule: Stripe is the source of truth for SUBSCRIPTION FACTS. Uellix is the source of truth for COMMERCIAL STATE and for ENTITLEMENT. The webhook reports a fact; the state machine decides what the fact means; the entitlement writer decides what the decision costs.
source_of_truth.consequence: A Stripe status is never stored AS the commercial state. It is stored as an observed subscription fact (FUTURE_DDL.D-7) and MAPPED. The mapping is enumerated in COMMERCIAL_STATE_MACHINE and is the only place the two vocabularies meet.
source_of_truth.why_not_store_stripe_status_directly: Stripe's vocabulary has no BOOTSTRAP and no ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE, because Stripe has no concept of a tenant that is commercially live without Stripe. Adopting Stripe's set would make OD-6 and OD-7 unrepresentable - the same failure mode as MC-1, imported instead of inherited.

WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-1_persist: source_event_created_at timestamptz NOT NULL is written at CLAIM time from the signed event's created field, into stripe_webhook_events. It joins event_id and event_type in the never-rewritable set (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:307 - what arrived cannot be rewritten). received_at is retained and is NEVER used for ordering.
WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-2_scope: The ordering scope is the STRIPE OBJECT the event addresses: stripe_subscription_id when present, else stripe_customer_id. Ordering is per object, never global - two subscriptions of one account are independently ordered, and a global order would make an unrelated event stale.
WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-3_regression_refusal: An event whose source_event_created_at is STRICTLY LESS than that of the most recent COMPLETED event in the same ordering scope is REFUSED as stale_event, marked terminally ignored, and answered 200. 200 and not 503: redelivery cannot make an event newer, so inviting redelivery would be an infinite refusal loop. This is the one place this authority departs from the handler's blanket-503 rule (lib/capabilities/stripe-webhook.ts:337-341), and it departs deliberately, because that rule exists to protect UNFINISHED work and a stale event is finished.
WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-4_equal_timestamp: event.created has second granularity, so two distinct events in one scope CAN share it. Where source_event_created_at is EQUAL and event_id differs: apply in arrival order IF and ONLY IF the resulting transition is legal and non-regressive under the transition table. A transition that would move commercial state BACKWARDS at an equal timestamp is REFUSED as ambiguous_order and ESCALATES. Fail closed: an ambiguity the data cannot resolve is not resolved by guessing.
WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-5_duplicate: A duplicate event_id is absorbed by the existing PRIMARY KEY. A duplicate of an event already completed is a NO-OP: nothing is re-applied, no second audit row is written, no grant is closed twice. stripe_begin_event's ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO UPDATE (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:530-534) is the existing carrier of this property and is preserved.
WEBHOOK_ORDERING.ORD-6_guard_is_a_precondition_not_a_chec: ORD-3 and ORD-4 are evaluated INSIDE the apply transaction, AFTER the per-account advisory lock is taken, in the same statement scope as the write. A guard evaluated before the lock is a guard two concurrent events can both pass. This is MC-3's amendment and it is the reason the unconditional UPDATE at db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:781-789 cannot simply be wrapped in an IF.

out_of_order_behaviour_summary.older_than_last_completed: REFUSED stale_event, terminal ignored, 200, no write, no audit beyond the ledger row.
out_of_order_behaviour_summary.newer: APPLIED subject to the transition table.
out_of_order_behaviour_summary.for_a_CLOSED_account: recorded, terminally ignored, cause account_closed - regardless of ordering.

PAST_DUE.decision: OD-4. Entering past_due has NO product effect while the relationship is recoverable.
PAST_DUE.what_changes: commercial_status becomes PAST_DUE. The persisted subscription status becomes past_due. An audit row records the transition. The tenant MAY be notified.
PAST_DUE.what_does_not_change: No grant is closed. No limit is reduced. No replacement grant is written. No capability becomes unavailable. organizations.status is untouched. Membership and roles are untouched.
PAST_DUE.recovery: An observed subscription active, or an observed paid invoice for the subscription, returns the account to ACTIVE_STRIPE. Because nothing was closed, recovery writes no grant either - it is a state transition with an empty entitlement effect in both directions.
PAST_DUE.escalation: Only an OBSERVED unpaid moves the account to SUSPENDED. Uellix runs no dunning clock of its own; Stripe's exhaustion of retries is the signal, and PAYMENT_SUSPENSION.grace_period's refusal to ratify a window is preserved rather than quietly filled in.
PAST_DUE.the_trap_this_clause_exists_to_close: The intuitive implementation of past_due is 'downgrade now, restore on payment'. It is wrong twice: it violates OD-4, and it makes recovery a GRANT REOPENING, which CE-3's append_only_rule forbids (a closed row is never un-closed; a restoration is a NEW row). Doing nothing on past_due is not laziness - it is the only shape that leaves the append-only invariant intact.

SUSPENSION.decision: OD-5. Observed unpaid closes commercial capacity.
SUSPENSION.closes: Every live PLAN grant for every Organization governed by the account. Each closure is explicit (effective_to set once), auditable (its own row naming the commercial cause) and reversible by policy (reinstatement is a NEW grant, never an un-closing).
SUSPENSION.retains: Sign-in, membership, roles, tenant identity, organizations.status, and READ access to all historical evidence, reports and audit history. PAYMENT_SUSPENSION.read_side_rule preserved.
SUSPENSION.gate: EC-4 sets the commercial gate to BLOCKED on entry, so the enforcement path is closed at the instant of the state write even though the grant closures land in a later transaction.
SUSPENSION.distinct_from_tenant_suspension: PI-1 preserved. organizations.status = 'suspended' is a different verb under a different authority and is measured at AS_OF to be inert (no tenant path compares it). This authority does not make it live and does not wire the two together.

CANCELLATION.decision: OD-6. Cancellation closes grant, transitions to the correct bootstrap / non-commercial state, and clears active subscription identity.
CANCELLATION.trigger: An observed customer.subscription.deleted, or an observed subscription status canceled.
effects_in_order: 2. Evaluate ORD-1..ORD-6. A stale cancellation is refused.
4. CLEAR stripe_subscription_id to NULL. RETAIN stripe_customer_id.
5. Emit the governed re-evaluation request (EC-3), in this same transaction.
7. In a SEPARATE transaction, the entitlement writer closes every live PLAN grant and opens BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT replacements where the capability catalogue declares one.

clearing_the_subscription_id_is_load_bea.measured_defect: db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:788 assigns stripe_subscription_id = COALESCE(p_stripe_subscription_id, stripe_subscription_id). The COALESCE was added for a good reason - a customer-addressed event with a NULL subscription argument used to silently DETACH the subscription, after which the subscription branch of the policy stopped matching and DP-CAP-15 forbade a webhook from re-binding it. But its effect is that a DELETION cannot clear the id either, because a deletion also arrives with the subscription argument that COALESCE preserves.
clearing_the_subscription_id_is_load_bea.consequence_if_unamended: A canceled subscription's id lingers, so re-subscription is ambiguous: the account looks like it still has a subscription that Stripe says is gone. F11 recorded this as gap (4).
clearing_the_subscription_id_is_load_bea.amendment: Clearing is EXPLICIT and TYPED. The cancellation path does not pass a NULL subscription argument and rely on COALESCE to do nothing; it invokes a distinct clearing act that sets the column to NULL as its stated purpose. The COALESCE protection on the ORDINARY update path is preserved untouched. A silent NULL and a stated NULL are different acts and must be different code.

CANCELLATION.no_free_10: EC-5. The cancellation path never consults a price resolver, so mapStripePriceToQuota(null) is never reached and the value 10 is unreachable from a cancellation by construction rather than by check.

REACTIVATION.same_subscription: An account in SUSPENDED whose SAME subscription is observed active returns to ACTIVE_STRIPE. Grants are re-opened as NEW rows of source PLAN (CE-3 append_only_rule: a closed row is never un-closed).
REACTIVATION.after_cancellation: An account in BOOTSTRAP re-subscribing goes through the FULL journey: the existing stripe_customer_id is reused (that is why cancellation retains it), a NEW checkout is created, a NEW subscription id is bound, and the state moves BOOTSTRAP -> ACTIVE_STRIPE. No first binding is repeated, because OD-2's idempotency key is the account and the account already has its customer.

subscription_replacement.definition: The account's live subscription id changes - an upgrade that Stripe implements as a new subscription, a migration between products, or a re-subscribe after cancellation.
subscription_replacement.rule: Exactly ONE subscription id may be live per CommercialAccount. A replacement CLOSES the outgoing subscription's commercial effect and OPENS the incoming one's, as one governed act under one lock, with one audit row naming both ids.
subscription_replacement.refusal: An event carrying a subscription id that is neither the live one nor NULL, for an account already carrying a different live subscription id, is REFUSED as subscription_conflict and ESCALATES. It is never applied by overwriting, because overwriting is indistinguishable from the cross-tenant binding attack seen from the inside.
subscription_replacement.unique_constraint: FUTURE_DDL.D-2's UNIQUE(stripe_subscription_id) makes a replacement that forgets to clear the outgoing id fail at the database rather than produce two accounts claiming one subscription.

REACTIVATION.plan_change_within_one_subscription: A price change on the SAME subscription is a self-transition ACTIVE_STRIPE -> ACTIVE_STRIPE. It emits a re-evaluation exactly like any other transition; the plan write and the grant write remain two acts (PLAN_ENTITLEMENT_BOUNDARY, preserved). Re-evaluation is DETERMINISTIC given (plan_ref, catalogue, organization), so a replay is a no-op rather than a second grant.

MANUAL_ACTIVATION.decision: OD-7. ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE only by explicitly authorized manual activation.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.sole_locus: CE-8, the Platform Admin commercial control plane. No tenant-facing surface, no self-service path and no webhook may reach this state. CE-8 depends_on CE-2, CE-3, CE-5 and externally on tenancy S5; manual activation is therefore NOT implementable before those close, and this authority does not pretend otherwise.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.eligibility: ONLY from BOOTSTRAP, and only when stripe_subscription_id IS NULL. An account with a live subscription - in any state including SUSPENDED - is INELIGIBLE. An operator extending capacity to a tenant with a live subscription uses a COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION grant, which is an entitlement act, not a state act.
mandatory_inputs: actor_user_id NOT NULL - a person. Machine-originated manual activation is a contradiction and is refused.
reason, non-empty, recorded verbatim in the audit row.
authorization_reference - the platform-admin decision identity, which is also the idempotency key.
review horizon - the date by which the arrangement must be renewed or it lapses to BOOTSTRAP.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.entitlement_source: COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION, with commercial_account_id NOT NULL. CE-3's CHECK constraints make the other three sources structurally wrong here: PLAN and COMMERCIAL_EXCEPTION require a non-NULL commercial_account_id and PLATFORM_ADMIN and BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT require it NULL - and an off-Stripe commercial arrangement HAS a commercial basis, so PLATFORM_ADMIN would lose exactly the fact that matters.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.no_unaudited_override: PAYMENT_SUSPENSION preserved: 'There is no unaudited override.' Every manual activation, renewal, and deactivation writes its own audit row with actor and reason.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.lapse: The review horizon expiring transitions the account to BOOTSTRAP by the same governed path as any other transition, with a machine actor and reason manual_activation_lapsed. A lapse is a transition, not a deletion, and it is auditable like any other.
MANUAL_ACTIVATION.measured_precondition: Both existing admin override surfaces call stella_0011 definers applied in NO database and raise 42883 at AS_OF (R-13). Manual activation cannot be delivered by extending a surface that does not execute.

STELLA_RECONCILIATION.principle: Three limits govern a Stella call. They are enforced at three different moments, by three different owners, for three different reasons, and they produce three different refusals. Conflating any two of them makes at least one unenforceable.

L1_technical_rate_limit.purpose: Protect the platform and the provider from burst load and abuse.
L1_technical_rate_limit.measured_posture: Distributed backend REQUIRED on staging and production; without it the function returns reason 'unavailable' and allowed false. In development, test and ci an in-memory Map fallback is retained and warned once. The module's own header records WHY: a per-instance Map on serverless gives one organization N times the limit, with N unknowable from inside the process.
L1_technical_rate_limit.enforced_when: At issuance, BEFORE any reservation. lib/stella/rate-limit.ts's header records that the only caller is issueGovernedStellaTicket and that issuance precedes reservation, so a rate-limited call mints no ticket, holds no quota unit and makes no provider call.
L1_technical_rate_limit.refusal_code: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, and RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE when the backend is absent in an environment that requires it.
L1_technical_rate_limit.commercial_status: NEVER SOLD. It is not a plan feature, is not an entitlement, is not a grant, and MUST NOT appear in the capability catalogue. An account that pays more does not get a higher rate limit by paying; if a higher rate limit is ever sold, it becomes a capability with its own grant and STOPS being L1.

L2_usage_quota.what: The monthly Stella capacity ledger and its reservations: uellix_stella.stella_capacity (prepared stella_0016), decided in exactly one place, bind_operation_ticket.
L2_usage_quota.owner: The Stella governed consumption chain, stella_0013..0018.
L2_usage_quota.purpose: Meter and reserve the units actually consumed.
L2_usage_quota.measured_posture: Organization-scoped, taken under a per-organization advisory lock, reserving in the same statement. lib/stella/quota.ts records that checkStellaQuota was REMOVED because it had no lock, no reservation awareness and was advisory only, and that readStellaCapacity is now an INFORMATIONAL reader that authorizes nothing.
L2_usage_quota.enforced_when: At binding, under the lock, in the same statement as the reservation.
L2_usage_quota.commercial_status: The LEDGER is not commercial. The LIMIT it compares against is. USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY, preserved: 'The LIMIT becomes a projection of the live EntitlementGrant; the LEDGER stays exactly where the prepared chain puts it.'

L3_commercial_entitlement.what: The live EntitlementGrant for (organization, stella capability), CE-3.
L3_commercial_entitlement.owner: The CE-5 governed entitlement writer, single-writer.
L3_commercial_entitlement.purpose: Answer whether the capability is purchased or allowed for this Organization, and up to what limit.
L3_commercial_entitlement.projection: limit_kind UNMETERED -> stella_monthly_quota NULL; BLOCKED -> 0; CAPPED -> limit_value. Written by the entitlement writer and by nobody else. USAGE_QUOTA_BOUNDARY.limit_projection, preserved.
L3_commercial_entitlement.gate: Conjoined with the commercial state gate of EC-4, which can only reduce.
L3_commercial_entitlement.refusal_code: entitlement_absent when no live grant exists; entitlement_blocked when the grant or the gate yields BLOCKED. DISTINCT from quota_exceeded: 'you have no allowance' and 'you have spent your allowance' are different facts and a tenant shown the wrong one cannot act correctly.
L3_commercial_entitlement.measured_gap: No grant exists at AS_OF; the limit's live source is organizations.stella_monthly_quota, assigned MANUALLY by a super_admin, defaulting to 0. L3 becomes real at CE-5 and is a manual assignment until then.

STELLA_RECONCILIATION.the_three_refusals_must_stay_three: A single generic refusal would make L1's platform protection indistinguishable from L2's exhausted allowance and from L3's absent purchase. The tenant's correct next action differs in each case: wait, buy more, or buy at all. Collapsing them is a product defect wearing an implementation shortcut.
STELLA_RECONCILIATION.display_consistency: A display surface reads readStellaCapacity, which is reservation-aware, so a screen and a refusal cannot tell a user two different stories. F10 measured that the billing page counts stella_interactions directly while enforcement uses stella_capacity - two numbers that can disagree. That divergence is closed by CB-7, not by this sentence.

RLS.measured_state: commercial_accounts: ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, ZERO policies (db/migrations/0068_commercial_account_ce1.sql:44-45). FORCE binds the table owner, so a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by the owner is equally locked out. This is the first application table in the repository to combine ENABLE + FORCE with zero policies and its migration header states the choice is deliberate.
RLS.the_problem_this_creates: OD-1 requires a canonical state machine over this column. A state machine needs a transition writer. At AS_OF no role can write, and the two ways out are both refused by existing doctrine: BYPASSRLS is asserted false as a postcondition for capability roles (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:938), and an owner-privileged definer is defeated by FORCE.

decision.shape: A dedicated capability LOGIN-less role, admitted by a RESTRICTIVE policy bound to a session GUC that the governed verb sets, exactly mirroring the cap_stripe_only_claimed_org pattern of stella_0008 (which binds writes to app.stripe_event_id).
decision.guc: app.commercial_account_id, set with set_config(..., true) so it is transaction-local and cannot leak across statements.
decision.predicate: The policy admits a row only when its id equals the GUC. The verb sets the GUC to the single account it is acting on, so the capability can write ONE row per transaction and cannot reach a second.
decision.grants: Column-scoped, exactly as stella_0008 does. commercial_status, stripe_customer_id, stripe_subscription_id, the subscription-fact columns and updated_at are UPDATE-able. id and created_at are NOT.
decision.zero_tenant_reach_preserved: This policy is an ACTOR bound, not a TENANT bound. It grants no membership, no role, no organization visibility and no tenant-facing read. The migration header's claim that commercial_accounts is NOT tenant data survives intact: nothing here makes it tenant-readable.
decision.no_tenant_read_policy_is_authored_here: A tenant-facing SELECT policy is NOT granted by this authority. If a billing screen must show commercial state, it reads it through a governed definer that returns a bounded projection, not through a policy that opens the table.

RLS.this_is_a_privilege_decision: F10 correctly classified adding a policy to this table as a privilege decision requiring authority rather than a fix. The authority is OD-1: a canonical state machine over a relation nothing may write is not a control. The DDL remains gated - FUTURE_DDL.D-6, LINEAGE_REDERIVATION_REQUIRED = YES.
RLS.entitlement_grants_rls: entitlement_grants is authored by CE-3 and its RLS posture is CE-3's to set. This authority adds no policy to it and states only the consumption rule: the evaluator takes an EXPLICIT organization_id and never an ambient principal (CE-3, preserved), which is what lets it be correct independently of whatever policy CE-3 chooses.

verbs: commercial.state.entered - every transition, from every cause. before_json and after_json carry the prior and new state; reason names the cause; entity_type is commercial_account.
commercial.stripe.bound - the first binding. Actor is the authenticated person who initiated it.
commercial.stripe.subscription_replaced - names BOTH the outgoing and incoming subscription ids.
commercial.manual_activation - actor MANDATORY non-NULL, reason MANDATORY, review horizon in after_json.
entitlement.grant.opened and entitlement.grant.closed - written by the CE-5 entitlement writer, NEVER by the state verb, each naming the commercial cause.
AUDIT.actor_rule: A Stripe-caused transition carries actor_user_id NULL. A person-caused transition carries a non-NULL actor. Both directions are enforced, not just one: db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:795-797 already refuses to attribute a billing change to a person who did not make it, and this authority adds the mirror - a manual activation MUST NOT be attributed to a machine.
AUDIT.two_rows_never_one: A state transition and its entitlement effect write SEPARATE audit rows in SEPARATE transactions. One row covering both would make the CC-3 fusion invisible again, and the separation is exactly what a reviewer checks to confirm PLAN_ENTITLEMENT_BOUNDARY held.
AUDIT.no_payload_in_the_ledger: stripe_webhook_events holds no payload and no error message, only a fixed error CODE. Preserved. source_event_created_at is an ordering identity, not a payload, and it is the only addition.
AUDIT.verbatim_content_caution: LANE HB measured that audit_logs before_json / after_json carries VERBATIM content in 40-plus verbs. The verbs above carry commercial state values, Stripe identifiers, a reason string and a review date. The reason string is operator-authored free text and is the only field of these verbs that can carry arbitrary content; an implementing node must treat it under whatever disclosure posture the audit surface adopts, and MUST NOT put a Stripe payload, an email body or a tenant record into it.

items.title: Governed re-evaluation request relation.
items.content: A relation recording (commercial_account_id, cause_identity, requested_at, consumed_at, outcome). Written by the state verb in the state transaction; consumed by the CE-5 entitlement writer in a separate one.
items.note: F12 measured ZERO queue, job, outbox or cron substrate, and INT-INT-001:39 explicitly discards an outbox. This relation is therefore NOT a general outbox and MUST NOT be argued into one. It is a single-purpose request log with a claim/lease/attempts shape, and the pattern to copy is stripe_webhook_events itself, which F12 identified as the repository's existing worked example.

FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.lock: A per-CommercialAccount advisory lock is taken before any state read that a write depends on, mirroring the per-organization lock of stella_0016 that lib/stella/quota.ts records as the fix for the read-then-write race.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.lock_ordering: Where both an account lock and an organization lock are needed, the ACCOUNT lock is taken FIRST, always. A fixed global order is what makes deadlock structurally impossible rather than rare.
transaction_boundaries: T1 state transaction: ledger completion + commercial state write + subscription-fact write + re-evaluation request row + state audit row. Atomic.
T2 entitlement transaction: grant closures and openings + entitlement audit rows + legacy projection write. Atomic, separate, idempotent by the request's cause_identity.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.why_two_transactions: STRIPE_BOUNDARY.downstream_reaction prohibits one transaction that both records a subscription and moves a quota, regardless of code factoring. Two transactions is not an optimisation; it is the boundary.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.the_window_between_them: Closed by EC-4's conjunctive gate, which is evaluated from commercial_status at enforcement time. T1 having committed is sufficient for the gate to close, so the window between T1 and T2 fails CLOSED rather than open.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.T2_failure: If T2 fails, the request row stays unconsumed and is retried. The gate keeps the account closed meanwhile. Repeated failure ESCALATES; it does not silently leave a suspended tenant with live grants, because the gate does not depend on T2 having run.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.T1_failure: The ledger row remains 'processing' and the handler answers 503, inviting redelivery. stripe_fail_event marks it failed from the handler's catch block AFTER the apply has raised and rolled back - the existing separation (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:43-46, 854-885) that exists precisely because an UPDATE followed by a RAISE in one transaction rolls its own bookkeeping back. Preserved.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.concurrent_events_same_account: Serialized by the advisory lock. The loser re-reads state inside its own lock hold and then evaluates ORD-3 and ORD-4 against the winner's committed result, which is why ORD-6 requires the guard to be inside the lock.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.concurrent_first_bindings: Serialized by the lock; the loser observes a non-NULL stripe_customer_id and returns it as a NO-OP. Should the lock ever be bypassed, UNIQUE(stripe_customer_id) refuses the second write. Should the API call itself be duplicated, the Stripe idempotency key keyed on commercial_account_id returns the same customer. Three independent bounds.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.partial_multi_org_application: An account governing N Organizations applies its entitlement effect N times. T2 is atomic across all N: a state change that lands for some Organizations and not others is PROHIBITED. If N is large enough that one transaction is impractical, the request row is split per Organization with per-Organization idempotency, and the gate of EC-4 keeps every not-yet-applied Organization correct in the meantime.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.escalation_means: STOP and surface. An escalating condition (ambiguous_order, subscription_conflict, manual_basis_conflict, binding collision, repeated T2 failure) is never auto-resolved, never guessed, and never silently retried into a different outcome. Fail closed where authority is ambiguous.
